brief: GS morning market-colour wrap across US and Europe equities, flows and single-name calls. SPX closed -2bps at 7704 Thursday, intraday strength linked to Strait of Hormuz headlines. META rose 4.5% on the Connect event and Muse momentum, now +25% since its Sep 8 launch. Asset managers were $500mm net sellers, supply in consumer discretionary and communication services against demand in macro products and healthcare. Hedge funds were net buyers, demand in communication services, macro products, energy and tech. Hyperscalers are tracking $800bn in 2026 AI capex and a consensus $1.1trn in 2027, needing about $300bn in annual AI revenue to break even. AI users would need to spend about $1trn a year on AI applications for hyperscalers to earn solid returns, versus $1.5trn in global software spending. Cross-asset: duration offers less reliable protection than before COVID given inflation volatility, fiscal risk and less negative equity/bond correlation, and favors best-carry curve segments. Essilor estimates are cut (revenue -40 to -170bps, EBIT/EPS -6% to -7% FY26-28e) on a more conservative AI-glasses ramp after Meta's own-branded launch. Europe pension reform: a EUR139-184bn AVD opportunity carries limited year-5 EPS impact (+/-0.5%) on insurers, from slow CSM earnings release and diversified books.
